searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight; two left unspent. Several restricted to the VDP, the houses or a house and the VDP. No fetch tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: dates, people, classification, grapes, sites, making, window, temperature, label words, story beats, cards and questions; then the house rules.

What mattered most: the Juliusspital site figures were not the VDP's, the Fürst restoration of 2010 was the official register and not the VDP, two harp and cask stories had no source, and several claims of rank were cut.

tested: Am Lumpen 1655 on the VDP's own page: field name first recorded in 1655 in a description of goods and regulations, which gives the Grosse Lage its name; south (S, SSW to SSE), about 60 per cent within a band of 35 to 70, 200 to 270 metres, upper shell limestone, an amphitheatre open to the Main. Kept, with the height and soil added.
Membership of the VDP from 2001: the VDP's estate page. Kept.
The Hütte planted in 1971 by the founder and his father: the house's own page only. Kept as the house tells it.

The making: the house's shop sheet (natural settling, wild yeasts, no cultured yeast, lees to the end of July) and its news page (all its GGs on their own yeasts). Selection and gentle pressing not found, cut.
Rainer Sauer as a separate Escherndorf house bottling an Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG: Falstaff, Vinmonopolet and a trade site. Kept.
Label form 'Escherndorf am Lumpen 1655': the house's shop, Falstaff, Meininger. Kept.
changed: wine.sites: 'vines more than thirty five years old' is cut (not found by the refuter); the VDP's figures are added, about 200 to 270 metres and upper shell limestone, with the amphitheatre's shelter from the north wind; was 'a slope of about sixty per cent facing south ... on shell limestone, with vines more than thirty five years old'; VDP Vineyard.Online, Am Lumpen 1655.

wine.making: 'selected in the vineyard and pressed very gently' is cut as unsourced; now the house's sheet alone (natural settling, wild yeasts, fine lees to the end of July) and the house's news page that all its GGs ferment with their own yeasts.
sources: the importer's page is replaced by Falstaff's listing of Weingut Rainer Sauer's Escherndorf am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG, which bears out the trap and the label form.
open: The Hütte planted in 1971 by the founder and his father rests on the house's own page alone, told as the house tells it; no independent source was found.
The VDP calls the record of 1655 a description of goods and regulations; Rainer Sauer's account calls it a wine tax document. The record follows the VDP.

sourcesRead.title: Falstaff: Weingut Rainer Sauer, Am Lumpen 1655 Silvaner GG

tested: Foundation stone of 12 March 1576 and the charter of 12 March 1579 endowing fields, vineyards and forests: a museum document, a Würzburg university folder and Wikipedia; Wines of Germany says 12 May 1576. Kept with the year.
Julius Echter, Prince Bishop from 1573, 1545 to 1617: the Deutsche Biographie and the Oxford cabinet page title (1573 to 1617). Kept.

The Stein-Berg on the VDP's own page: 190 to 280 metres, 30 to 75 per cent, middle shell limestone, the greater part shared by the three Würzburg estates. The author's 210 to 285 metres and terraces were not the VDP's: corrected.
The relief and the Bocksbeutel: Wines of Germany and Wikipedia; the flask may have been a medicine flask. Reworded.
The cellar's 220 oak casks: the foundation's own page; cooling plates and oak from its own forests not found, cut.
The Stein-Berg label: Falstaff lists a 2019 Würzburg Stein-Berg Silvaner GG and a 2015 Würzburg Stein Silvaner GG; dated from about 2019.
changed: wine.sites: was 'facing south to south east at 210 to 285 metres, mostly terraced and steep, on weathered shell limestone with clay loam that throws light back onto the vines'; now the VDP's figures, 30 to 75 per cent and 190 to 280 metres on middle shell limestone, with the Stein-Berg's three chief owners; the aspect and the light were not found and are cut.

wine.making: 'some of them coopered from oak of the foundation's own forests and fitted with cooling plates' is cut, not found; now the house's own count of some 220 oak casks in the historic cask cellar, with barriques and tonneaux beside them.

story: 'A stone charter carved in 1576 shows the gifts, and Wines of Germany notes a Bocksbeutel among them' is now the relief of the foundation with a flask some read as an early Bocksbeutel, perhaps a medicine flask, as Wines of Germany and Wikipedia give it; 'the cellar under the hospital dates from the foundation' is cut, not found.
wine.label, story and traps: the Stein-Berg name is dated from about the 2019 vintage, was 2020: Falstaff lists a 2019 Würzburg Stein-Berg Silvaner GG and a 2015 Würzburg Stein Silvaner GG.
table and cards: 'terraces' and 'clay loam' are gone with the site line; now steep shell limestone.
open: The foundation stone is 12 March 1576 in the foundation's history and a museum document, 12 May 1576 in Wines of Germany; the record gives the year only in prose but the day is the foundation's.
The aspect of the Stein-Berg was not read in any source.

sourcesRead.title: Falstaff: Juliusspital 2019 Würzburg Stein-Berg Silvaner GG

tested: 1316, Johannes von Steren and Mergardis: Wikipedia and the charters of the Stadtarchiv Würzburg on monasterium.net; the house marked 700 years in 2016. Kept, founders described.
The Stein-Harfe a VDP Grosse Lage in sole ownership in the heart of the Stein: the house's pages and Valckenberg. Kept.
The harp of path and rows and the spelling Harpfe of the seventeenth century: not found; a glossary reads the name as stony ground. Cut.
The making: the house's sheets of 2016 (steel), 2018 (wood), 2023, 2024 and 2025 (long skin contact, wild fermentation in Stück or wooden cask, fine lees). Now the 2024 sheet.
1726 and the 1718 vintage sealed with the city's seal: the house's catalogue, the city's portal and Wines of Germany. Kept.
1665 Silvaner in the Stein by a Cistercian abbot: Wikipedia's Würzburger Stein; Wines of Germany ties the grape to Ebrach's monks. Kept, abbot unnamed.
The sweet Stein-Harfe Riesling Spätlese: the house's catalogue (2023) and Falstaff (2018). Added to others.
changed: wine.sites, story and cards: the name Harpfe of the seventeenth century and the harp drawn by the path and rows are cut, not found (a glossary reads the name as stony ground); the site is now named as the house names it, stone harp in English, with old vines on steep shell limestone.

wine.making: now the house's sheet of the 2024 vintage: long skin contact, wild fermentation in wooden casks, the Stück among them, fine lees in wood; the 2016 sheet gives cool fermentation in steel, so the method is not timeless.
others: adds the Stein-Harfe Riesling Spätlese the plan asked for, found on the house's catalogue and Falstaff; card 1 now asks for it.
sources: Tageskarte and the 2018 sheet give way to the house's 2024 sheet and the city of Würzburg's page on the Bocksbeutel, which gives the sealing from the 1718 vintage.
open: The sealing of the 1718 vintage rests on Wines of Germany, the city's portal and the house's own account; no archival study was read.
The founders' dates (Johannes von Steren, about 1270 to 1329) are in Wikipedia alone; the founders stay described, not named.

tested: 1638: wein.plus, Wines of Germany and the house. Kept.
1979 estate house in the Centgrafenberg: wein.plus; one source puts a handover in 1979. Kept as the house.

The Hundsrück: tax classified in 1564 (VDP), folded into the Centgrafenberg in 1971 (VDP), entered again in the official register in 2010 (VDP and the house), south, about 35 per cent, 170 to 230 metres, weathered Buntsandstein. The author's 'the VDP has listed it again' corrected.
The making: open wooden vats, high share of whole bunches up to all, basket press, 228 litre barrels, unfiltered; 13 to 18 months (English page) and 12 to 20 (German). Kept, hedged.
Klingenberger Schlossberg GG (VDP: Buntsandstein, Spätburgunder only) and the Centgrafenberg Frühburgunder (Falstaff 2014, wein.plus 2010; later labelled R). Kept.
changed: story: 'Since 2010 the VDP has listed the Hundsrück again' is wrong in kind: it was entered again in Franken's official register of vineyards in 2010 (the VDP's own page and the house's); now so, with card 2.

story: 'one of the German pioneers of red wine raised in small Burgundian barrels' and 'made the Mainviereck known as red wine country' are cut as claims of rank with no second source; 'By 2016, as a trade profile ... more whole bunches' is now the house's own pages: open wooden vats, often a high share of whole bunches.
wine.sites: adds the VDP's slope of about 35 per cent and the eastern parcels of the Bürgstadter Berg; 'red to orange' is cut.
wine.making: the share of whole bunches is now the house's 'high share, at times all of them'.
open: The house also cites a document of 1525 naming the Hundsrück; the record keeps the VDP's tax record of 1564.
The new estate house of 1979 is in wein.plus and Wines of Germany; another trade source puts a handover in 1979.

tested: 6 April 1659, 25 Austrian cuttings at the foot of the Schlossberg: the house, Wines of Germany, Valckenberg; Wikipedia gives 5 April. Kept, hedged.
1224 and Ebrach: Wines of Germany and Valckenberg. Kept.
About 1266, the counts' division charter naming the Schlossberg, Hohnart, Reitsteig and Trautberg: the VDP's own page; the division itself in the Göttingen Academy's lexicon. Kept, sharpened.
1057: the Göttingen lexicon names a presumed earliest ancestor in 1057. Reworded.
The Schlossberg: VDP, sole ownership, 40 to 70 per cent, 340 to 370 metres, Gipskeuper with gypsum, alabaster and blue clay shale, west (south and west on the English page). Added.
The making and the span: the house's sheets (light skin contact, spontaneous fermentation, Casteller wood; ten to thirty years in 2018, up to twenty in 2020). Span corrected.
changed: wine.sites: adds the VDP's slope of 40 to 70 per cent, the westward aspect (the house's sheet and the VDP's German page; the English page says south and west) and some 340 to 370 metres.
wine.ageing: 'the house gives it a span of ten to thirty years' is now up to twenty, thirty in some vintages: the 2018 sheet says ten to thirty, the 2020 sheet up to twenty.
story: the ancestor of 1057 is now a presumed ancestor, as the Göttingen Academy's lexicon has it; the division of about 1266 now names the Schlossberg and the Hohnart, as the VDP's page reads.

others: the Hohnart's 'aged a year on its lees in Castell oak' and the Kugelspiel's 'partly in casks, partly in steel' are cut as unsourced; the Kugelspiel is now named an Erste Lage as the house's sheet titles it.
open: The planting of 6 April 1659 is the house's archive, borne out by Wines of Germany and the importer; Wikipedia gives 5 April. Told as the house's account.
The house says it holds its GGs five years in the castle cellar before release; not added, as one sheet only.

livingNamesNote: Horst Sauer and Rainer Sauer are living and are house names; the prose uses them only as the houses. None of the six is in people.json; the read-together agent may add them.

swaps.note: The author proposed no swap. The report mused on the Iphöfer Julius-Echter-Berg for the Juliusspital without proposing it; the refuter sees no reason to: the Stein is the hill the foundation is known by, and the Julius-Echter-Berg stays in others.

codexInTension.note: The GG now carries the Grosse Lage Am Lumpen 1655 on its label (the house's shop, Falstaff, the VDP); the library's name is the older, wider one. Reported, not edited.

codexInTension.says: Escherndorfer Lump is an Einzellage, not a Grosslage
codexInTension.note: True, but the VDP now classes its heart as the Grosse Lage Am Lumpen 1655; a reader may confuse Grosse Lage with Grosslage. Reported, not edited.

plan.whys: The burgerspital pick's why says its Stein-Harfe Rieslings are sweet: the house sells a Stein-Harfe Riesling Spätlese and Auslese, borne out; no change asked. The furst note asked when the Hundsrück was first bottled alone: not found, left open.
